task.description:
RECONSTRUCTED BY ORCH, 2026-09-04, and labelled as such rather than presented as agent-written. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR executed this gate and reported its verdict in full, but did NOT write this handoff file to disk. CODE-DESIGNER discovered the absence at the start of rework 1 and reported it rather than silently working around it -- correct behaviour, and the reason this gap was caught at all. ORCH's own step-02b GATE_FAIL log entry and commit had cited this file as though it existed, which was wrong; this reconstruction closes that audit hole. Content below is taken from the validator's reported verdict, plus ORCH's own independent empirical re-verification of both findings. It is NOT a verbatim agent artifact and must not be read as one.

HARD GATE on CODE-DESIGNER's template-clone design for ISS-0427. The failure mode under gate is SILENT: a cloned tenant schema subtly non-equivalent to a migration-built one would weaken every tenant-dependent test in the suite without failing anything visibly.

result.summary:
FAIL -- 1 BLOCKER, 1 MAJOR.

BLOCKER: design section 3.2 dimension 3 groups pg_constraint by contype over {c,f,p,u} and asserts in bold that this is 'the full set Postgres defines'. It is not -- Postgres also defines x (exclusion constraints) and t (constraint triggers). A clone missing an exclusion constraint would pass the parity check untouched, since the grouping never inspects contype='x' and none of the other 7 dimensions covers it. ORCH INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: created an EXCLUDE constraint and confirmed pg_constraint.contype='x' is real and outside the asserted-exhaustive four.

MAJOR: table-level storage parameters (pg_class.reloptions -- fillfactor, autovacuum_* overrides) are silently uncovered. INCLUDING ALL's INCLUDING STORAGE copies only per-column attstorage, a different concept. Unlike triggers/comments/collations/privileges -- which the design explicitly enumerated and ruled out with stated reasons -- reloptions is simply absent, neither covered nor consciously excluded. ORCH INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: a template table WITH (fillfactor=70) clones to a table whose pg_class.reloptions is EMPTY.

VERIFIED CORRECT AND NOT TO BE RE-LITIGATED IN REWORK: the FK textual rewrite is correct on every adversarial shape tried (self-referencing, composite, DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, ON DELETE/ON UPDATE CASCADE -- pg_get_constraintdef embeds deferrability and referential actions natively); sequence recreation is correct end-to-end (clone-local sequence, default repointed, OWNED BY set, starts at 1 rather than inheriting the template's counter); the index-rename finding reproduces exactly and the structural-not-name-based comparison is the right call; template-name collision safety verified live (tenant_id_for_schema_name('tenant_template') returns {:error, :invalid_schema_name}); the reaper structurally cannot drop the template because INV-4 guarantees no tenant_schemas row exists for it, though the design never states this and should; scope is clean with zero lib/ diff; OQ-1 is an acceptable open question with two fully-specified options; and the speedup claim is honest as written (an order-of-magnitude check suggests ~2.3x for the full mechanism rather than 2.5x, consistent with the design's own hedging).

All validator probe schemas were dropped and confirmed gone.

issues.title: Parity check's pg_constraint contype enumeration {c,f,p,u} is asserted exhaustive but omits x (exclusion) and t (constraint trigger)
issues.description: A degraded clone missing an exclusion constraint passes the check unseen. Independently confirmed by ORCH against a live Postgres catalog.

issues.title: Table-level storage parameters (pg_class.reloptions) are uncovered by the parity check and not copied by LIKE INCLUDING ALL
issues.description: Verified by ORCH: fillfactor=70 on the template yields empty reloptions on the clone. Neither covered nor explicitly ruled out, unlike the design's treatment of triggers/comments/collations/privileges.
